subtopic: Moving to a new city on limited money
subtype: Approach: sign the first flat to end the stress [Pitfall]
passage: My name is Tushar, and by the fifth week of flat hunting in Hyderabad I was exhausted. Every evening after work I looked at listings until my eyes hurt. Then a broker sent a video of a flat that looked fine, and I said, "I'll take it." I handed over the broker's charge plus a hefty deposit that afternoon, without seeing the place. Sabina had told me on the phone to go and look first. I told her I was too tired. The flat turned out to be an hour and ten minutes from my office, and the lease said I could not leave for eleven months. I had chosen the way one grabs a chair after standing too long, and I paid for it every day.

qa.q: How long was the journey from the flat to the office?
qa.a: The flat was an hour and ten minutes from the office.

qa.q: Why did Tushar say I'll take it after seeing the video?
qa.a: Tushar felt worn out by five weeks of searching and wanted the stress to end, so tiredness decided the choice.

qa.q: What could Tushar do now about the lease, and why?
qa.a: Tushar could read the lease again and ask the owner about options, because a written agreement shows what can still be changed.

qa.q: How might Sabina see the call when Sabina advised looking first?
qa.a: Sabina was probably worried and may now feel frustrated that the advice was not followed, but might offer help.

grounding: Worn out by searching, a newcomer pays a broker fee and a large deposit for a flat seen only on video, which turns out to be far from work with strict lease terms.

passage:
Supervisor's note, week 3. Bhavna, new-joiner buddy lead.
Mohit has been late four times in his first three weeks. Today I asked why. He looked exhausted. He had spent his first ten days in the city hunting for a flat after work, seeing places until midnight. On the eleventh night a broker sent a video of a clean one-room flat, and Mohit sent the broker ₹15,000, plus a ₹60,000 deposit, online without visiting. 'I just wanted it to be over,' he said.
The flat is in Wagholi. Our office is in Hinjewadi. His commute is two hours each way. The lease has an eleven-month lock-in; if he leaves early, he loses two months of the deposit.
I've moved his start time to 10:30 for now, and put him in touch with the company's housing help desk to go through the lease terms properly. I'll review with him at week 6.

qa.q: How much did Mohit send the broker?
What does 'I just wanted it to be over' reveal about Mohit?
qa.a: He was worn out and desperate for the stress to end, so tiredness decided instead of checking.

qa.q: What could Mohit have done on the eleventh night instead?
qa.a: Asked to visit before paying, or booked a short stay for a few more days, so the choice was not made in exhaustion.

qa.q: How does the situation look to Bhavna, who wrote the note?
qa.a: Bhavna sees lateness caused by a tired choice, not carelessness, and responds with a later start time and housing help.

grounding: Shows a worn-out newcomer paying a broker fee and big deposit for a flat seen only on video, ending up far from work with a strict lease.

passage:
Friday, 11:50 p.m. Ira's diary.
Two weeks of flat-hunting in Chennai after work, and tonight I gave up and said yes to the one in the video. Broker fee ₹12,000. Deposit ₹70,000, which is basically everything Amma gave me plus my first salary. I sent it at 9 p.m. from the office washroom because the broker said someone else was coming at ten.
Moving in tomorrow. More after.
Sunday, 10 p.m.
The video didn't show the main road. Or that it's an hour and twenty minutes to the office by two buses. The agreement says eleven months, no early exit without losing the deposit. I read it only today.
Farhan came to help carry boxes, looked at the two buses on the map, and didn't say anything, which was worse.
I was so tired I wanted anyone to decide for me. The broker did.

qa.q: What does 'I wanted anyone to decide for me' reveal about Ira?
qa.a: Ira was exhausted after two weeks of searching, and that tiredness handed the decision to the broker.

qa.q: What could Ira do now about the lease?
qa.a: Ask a trusted adult or someone who knows rental agreements whether any exit is possible, and look for ways to ease the commute meanwhile.

qa.q: Why might Farhan stay silent looking at the map?
qa.a: Farhan probably sees how bad the commute is and does not want to rub it in when nothing can be undone that day.

grounding: Shows an exhausted newcomer paying a broker and large deposit for a flat seen only on video, which turns out far from work with a strict lease.
